inline_comments.comment:
`hasItems` is `false` whenever there are no built-in or user-tag entries, even if status items exist. Because the action bar — which contains the 'Clear filters' / 'Select all' button — is gated on `hasItems`, a user who has active status filters (e.g. set from the URL) but no tag entries has no way to clear them from the panel. Fix:
```ts
const hasItems = builtInItems.length > 0 || tagItems.length > 0 || statusItems.length > 0;
```

The parent-entry check scans only **direct** children (`item.parent === entry.id`). For trees deeper than two levels (e.g., a root group → component → story), a group node fails the status filter, its only direct children are intermediate components (which also fail), so the group is hidden even though a grandchild story would have passed. Either recurse through descendants or, better, pre-build a `parentId → descendant stories[]` map before the filter loop. The current approach is also O(M × N) — a full linear scan of `indexEntries` for each non-passing entry — which will degrade visibly on large indexes.

The selector was broadened from `svg + input` to `:not(input) + input` to handle the new `StatusIcon` (`<span>`). However, `:not(input) + input` matches **any** element immediately preceding an `<input>` — including buttons, divs, etc. — and could inadvertently hide inputs elsewhere in an `ActionList`. A more targeted alternative that covers the original and new cases without over-selecting: `'&:not(:hover, :has(:focus-visible)) :is(svg, span) + input'`.

This import reaches four directories deep into another package's internal implementation:
```ts
import type { Link } from '../../../components/components/tooltip/TooltipLinkList';
```
The project's guideline is to import through a package's public exports rather than deep relative paths, which are fragile under restructuring. Check whether `Link` is re-exported from a barrel file (e.g., `storybook/internal/components`) or add it there.

Import ordering is broken: local module imports (lines 9–11) appear before third-party type imports (lines 12–13). Per the project's import conventions, third-party/framework imports should come before local ones. Additionally, the `type` imports from `@storybook/react-vite` and `../../../manager-api` should be grouped with the other `import type` block at the top of the file rather than interleaved with value imports.

The `parseStatusesParam` and `serializeStatusesParam` describe blocks added here are **identical** to the ones already in `statuses.test.ts`. Duplicating them means any change to parsing/serialisation logic requires updating two files and makes failures ambiguous. Remove these two describe blocks from `stories.test.ts` — they already have thorough coverage in the dedicated `statuses.test.ts` file. The integration tests in this file should focus on how status filters interact with stories module state, not on re-testing pure utility functions.

Several `it()` bodies in the new `describe('computeStatusFilterFn (via experimental_setFilter)')` block call `vi.mock('../stores/status')` inline. Per the project's spy-mocking convention (`.cursor/rules/spy-mocking.mdc`), `vi.mock` calls must be at **module scope** (top level), not inside test bodies. Inline `vi.mock` calls may not be hoisted correctly by Vitest and can cause unpredictable behaviour across tests. Hoist the mock to the top of the file alongside the other module-level mock declarations.

`experimental_useStatusStore()` already returns `StatusesByStoryIdAndTypeId` by default (the generic `T` defaults to that type when no selector is passed). The `as StatusesByStoryIdAndTypeId` cast is therefore redundant and creates a misleading impression that a real type gap is being bridged. Remove the cast: `const allStatuses = experimental_useStatusStore();`.

The fallback `({ search: '' } as any)` silences TypeScript rather than handling the case properly. Since `queryFromLocation` already accepts `Partial<Location> | undefined` (its parameter is optional), the nullish-coalescing fallback can be removed entirely:
```ts
const { tags, statuses } = queryFromLocation(location);
```
If the intent is to guard against `location` being `undefined` in test environments, the real fix is to type `location` correctly in the init context rather than suppressing the error with `as any`.

general_comments.comment: **Status filter and the 'always-show-errors' rule can interact incorrectly.** In `stories.ts` (lib), the status filter runs first and returns `false` early for an entry (and its direct children). The subsequent 'always show errors' check at line 215 is then never reached for those entries. This is the stated intent — status filters take priority — but it means a user who *excludes* `status-value:error` will successfully hide error stories, which may be surprising and breaks the existing contract that error stories are always visible. This behavioural change should be prominently called out in docs/changelog so addon authors who rely on that guarantee are aware.

**Architectural inconsistency between the status filter and all other filter functions.** `computeStatusFilterFn` reads from `fullStatusStore.getAll()` (a global mutable singleton) inside the returned filter closure, making it an impure function. Every other filter (`STATIC_FILTER`, `TAGS_FILTER`, user-supplied filters) is a pure function of its arguments. This inconsistency makes the status filter harder to test in isolation and harder to reason about when filters are composed together. A cleaner approach would be to pass statuses through the entry (the transform function already does `{ ...entry, statuses }`) and have `computeStatusFilterFn` read from `entry.statuses` instead of the global store — similar to how the 'always show errors' rule already works.

**`setAllTagFilters` is called in `FilterPanel`'s 'Select all' path with built-in filter IDs (`_docs`, `_play`, `_test`) included in the list.** This works today because `computeTagsFilterFn` routes built-in IDs through `BUILT_IN_FILTERS`, but the caller of `setAllTagFilters` assembles `filterIds` from both `builtInEntries` and `tagEntries` without distinction. If a built-in filter ID is ever changed or removed from `BUILT_IN_FILTERS`, this silent coupling will cause `setAllTagFilters` to silently store a stale ID. Consider either separating the 'select all built-ins' and 'select all user tags' paths or adding an assertion/guard in `setAllTagFilters`.
